answer: One defense is vouching with liability: a new agent joins only when an established member stakes a bond on it, so trust spreads like a vine from rooted identities rather than appearing from nowhere. If a vouched agent is later caught colluding, the sponsor loses its stake too, so each fake identity costs the attacker real bond for every ledge it climbs onto, and a whisper of free registrations becomes impossible because every clone needs a backer willing to lose money.
